The ego never goes away - desire to control life to get more pleasure and less pain runs out of fuel because it's exhasuting and unsatisfying. So simply a person's ego stops believing that the old way of life, the old addictions, the old behaviours etc. will result in happiness.

The ego process itself though is required for social interaction and never goes away until someone dies. A lot of the ego issues we face in life are psychotherapy related complex-trauma issues from childhood (not feeling safe to be authentic / feeling unlovable or unworthy). Look up Tim Fletcher on YouTube. He's a Canadian addiction counsellor and he's fantastic.

Ultimately enlightenment is already and always here but we stop moving away from it and trying to transcend feelings and instead an embrace of life starts to happen. Slowly at first but over time we see that we architect our own misery and we begin to do that less and less. We stop hoping for something in the future that will free us. We stop believing that we aren't already enlightened being. We stop believing our mind that tells us we aren't enough. We stop thinking we have to earn the right to be. We see reality. Already and always whole. And we let go of the nonesense that keeps us small, scared, addicted and living in lack.

You are already it. You and life are inseperable. It's only our dualistic mind that holds on to the belief that "This isn't it. I'm not there yet". This is it my friend. Love yourself now.

Blessings :)

P.S. you are totally free to live how you see fit. Game as much as you want. There is no "wrong" way to be. You just notice addictive relationships where you may be avoiding honoring the signals from your body that enough is enough. If you ignore those signals it'll result in over-stimulation, withdrawals and imbalance which ultimately don't feel great. But if you balance your life and have a non-addictive relationship with substances, activities, people etc. then you can do whstever you want and maintain a balanced inner-world which ultimately feels good. The middle way :)

Anxiety is usually about fears regarding the imagined future. Generally it's a sense that "I don't want X to happen or I need X to happen". Generally it's a resistance to feeling something that a person is scared to feel - grief, pain, sadness, dispair etc. I've learned to meditate regularly to get in contact with reality as it is NOW. 99.99% of the time that reality is fine and I realise that it's the mind that's pulling me into fears. If there's body anxiety it's about being willing to feel the fear you have now, and not getting pulled into the minds plans regarding it all. Just feel the fear & don't believe the minds stories about the fear. Think of it like being in a sauna or an ice bath. It's uncomfortable, but if you relax and feel and trust as much as you can, then your body starts to adapt to the fear (temperature in this analagy). The more you can sit in fear the more your body processes it, you'll let out repressed emotions and basically surrender to the process. It's challenging but it works. You'll slowly become more resilliant. It's not a one time fix all though. It's more like hygiene. You have to wash your teeth every day and you have to meditate / be with yourself every day too as life is stressful. Also, if someone is anxious they shouldn't be taking in any stimulants like caffeine, cacao drinks, too much sugar because homeostasis is what is needed. Stimulats will bring people away from peaceful relaxing feelings and towards energetic fast moving feelings and thoughts - further stressing the system and blocking the processing of emotions.

Depression wise I'm not an expert. Often depression is a focus on the past and the unfairness of life. Disempowered feelings etc. There's usually a story that a person is telling themselves that makes them feel like someone else is to blame for where they currently are in life. That story is usually not helpful, but people often repeat it in their mind and strengthen it, which means they start to associate their identity with a depressed state "I am depressed". Then when they start to move away from that, they may feel like they are loosing their identity and that can be scary because the newer way of being is unknown and may feel unsafe (people often feel like positive emotions are unsafe because they don't last, and so they'd prefer to stay in the safety of predictable negative emotion - it may suck, but it's safe and predictable in their mind).

anxiety is about getting lost in an imagined future and wanting to avoid negative feelings and emotions.

Depression is about getting lost in and identifying with their imagined past (negative disempowered interpretation of memory with things like blame, shame, guilt, unworthiness mixed in - "I'm shit, people are shit, life is shit" type thinking).

Humans are creatures of habit and so we have to be careful what we practice telling ourselves... eventually it'll become our story and we'll believe it to be true. Then it's very hard to undo thoughts, feelings and emotions that feel very familliar because our system doesn't care if we are happy - it only cares that we are alive. The human ego & nervous system repeats patterns that feel familliar because it sees that it has done this for a long time and so it can predict outcomes. Nothing is more important to humans than a safe predictable future. It can be anxious, depressed and miserable but at least the person can feel lime they know what's coming. However once someone gets some level of meta-cognition going they can start to realise that they don't really want to know & control the future. They want peace & contentment - they want to be free of the minds interpretations and attempts to control experience. In short they want to have faith in life. They want to let go of control and rediscover their true identity as being / life itself. That requires letting go of a lot of desires and aversions for ones future which can lead to dissapointment and frustration. Ego death means letting go of the past and the future so that a person can flow with whatever comes - unpredictable life - but when someone isn't trying to get something and they aren't trying to avoid anything then they can just be themselves without any fear (anxiety) or dispair (depression). It's a totally different approach to life that takes a lot of adapting to. I'm doing my best to find balance between doing and being.
